findings.description: The new scrubber checks executable destinations without normalizing paths. For example, `tee /tmp/../etc/cron.d/job <<'EOF'` is classified as nonexec because `_bdb_hd_exec_dest` only recognizes the literal `/etc/` prefix. A body line `* * * * * root rm -rf /` is then discarded because its first word is `*`, hiding the destructive command from the guard.
findings.failure_mode: In a privileged session, the guard permits writing a destructive cron job that the previous full scan would detect. Equivalent paths bypass the intended executable-destination protection.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize destination paths before checking protected directories and PATH membership. If normalization cannot be established safely, retain the full body for scanning. Add a regression case covering a cron destination containing `/../`.

findings.description: Under implement_gate.mode: deny (documented as the only mode where the gate is a fence), a fresh .run/implement-active.json sanctions any App Zone write. The gate protects that file only against Write/Edit tool writes (trust-input ask). It is a PreToolUse:Write|Edit hook, so a Bash call (`run-checkpoint.sh mark implement S1`, or `printf '{"skill":"implement","sprint":"x","started_at":"<now>"}' > .run/implement-active.json`) creates a valid marker with no ask. The header spends considerable effort making model-authored active_skill claims tighten-only, yet the marker is equally model-authored via a different tool and grants an allow for two hours.
findings.failure_mode: In deny mode, a model that drifts outside /implement can self-sanction in one Bash call and then write to the App Zone freely with action=allow decision=sanctioned_marker rows, defeating the fence the operator opted into.
findings.suggested_fix: Either have run-checkpoint.sh mark record something the hook can corroborate (e.g. require the marker's sprint to match the RUNNING cache's current sprint and the cache to be fresh), make the marker only extend an already-known RUNNING position rather than stand alone, or document in guard-origins.yaml that deny is not a fence against a Bash-tool marker write and add a block-destructive-bash rule for writes to .run/implement-active.json.

findings.cross_file_justification: The new _ig_derived_ok call in check_implementation_active (both the sprint-plan-state.json and the state.json RUNNING branches) depends on run-checkpoint.sh refreshing derived_at during a run; run-checkpoint.sh is in the diff but not shown.
findings.description: check_implementation_active now returns 1 when the RUNNING cache carries a derived_at older than run_mode.stale_hours (default 12h), even though last_activity is fresh. _ig_within also rejects any ISO timestamp not ending in Z (e.g. `date -Iseconds` style `+00:00`) because jq fromdateiso8601 does not parse offsets, so such a derived_at is treated as stale. Whether every checkpoint refreshes derived_at (and in Z form) is not visible in this diff.
findings.failure_mode: A legitimate autonomous run longer than stale_hours, or one whose derived_at is written with a UTC offset, silently loses its sanction mid-run: every App Zone write starts asking (ask/telemetry/deny modes alike), with decision rows that look like drift. In run mode an unexpected ask can stall or halt the run.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm run-checkpoint.sh rewrites derived_at (UTC, trailing Z) on every checkpoint/record-round; have _ig_within normalize `+00:00`/`-00:00` to Z before fromdateiso8601; add a bats case for RUNNING + fresh last_activity + 13h-old derived_at documenting the intended outcome.

findings.cross_file_justification: profiles.yaml sets guardrails.danger_level.enforce and guardrails.input.enabled to false for lean and standard; danger-level-enforcer.sh and skill-includes/input_guardrails.md now read through loa_knob with a false fallback instead of the previous `// true` / skip-only-if-explicit-false semantics.
findings.description: Two safety surfaces flip from default-on to default-off for every repository that never set the key: danger-level enforcement (previously `// true`, and enabled when the config file was absent) and the pre-execution input guardrails (previously skipped only on an explicit false). The diff references DEC-0161 and calls it a migration item, but nothing in the diff warns an operator at session start or in /loa status that enforcement they relied on is now disabled unless loa.profile: full or the explicit key is set.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream repos upgrading the framework silently lose prompt-injection guardrails and danger-level enforcement on skill invocations with no log row or warning, while their .loa.config.yaml looks unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit a one-time WARN (session-start hook or loa-status Gate line) when loa.profile is unset and neither guardrails key is explicit, stating the effective value and how to restore it; or keep the explicit-false-only semantics for these two keys until the cycle-129 end flip.

findings.description: _bdb_hd_same_line_exec splits the line on `(` and `)` as pipeline separators and treats `cat` as a safe reader, so `cat <<'EOF' > a.txt … EOF; source <(cat a.txt)` or `bash <(cat a.txt)` yields segments `source <`, `cat a.txt` (safe) and never reports the target as executed. The heredoc stays nonexec and its body is reduced to fence-verb segments. The body-scan defense still keeps rm/git/find/… segments, so the gap only matters for destructive patterns the fence matches that do not start with a listed verb, but the classifier's own contract says a target named outside a safe reader is interpreter-class.
findings.failure_mode: A heredoc body routed into an executing consumer through process substitution of a safe reader is classified nonexec; any fence rule keyed on a command word outside _bdb_hd_is_destructive is not applied to that body.
findings.suggested_fix: In _bdb_hd_same_line_exec, return 0 (interpreter) when a line naming the target basename also contains `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(`, mirroring _bdb_hd_ctx_bad; add corpus cases for `source <(cat x)` and `bash <(cat x)`.

findings.description: For a nonexec heredoc, every body segment whose command word is not in _bdb_hd_is_destructive (rm git find dd shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql mkfs* DROP DELETE TRUNCATE) is dropped from the scrub copy before the normal rules run. The comment asserts this list equals 'command words the fence's own rules match', but the fence's rule set is not in the diff and the list is hand-maintained; any rule keyed on another word (e.g. chmod/chown -R, `> /dev/sd*`, crontab -r, helm uninstall, docker system prune via a non-interp path, wipefs/fdisk) no longer sees heredoc bodies, whereas pre-cycle it did for every non-cat consumer.
findings.failure_mode: A fence rule that fires on the pre-cycle full scan can be silently bypassed by placing the command in a heredoc fed to tee/gh/git commit, with no corpus failure if the corpus only covers the listed verbs.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the verb list from the rule table (or assert equality in tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/run-corpus.sh by extracting the leading command words from every fence regex), and add a corpus case per rule family that routes the payload through a nonexec heredoc body.

findings.description: All five C-TEAM constraints (lead-only planning skills, serialized br operations, lead-owned .run state files, lead-coordinated git, teammate System Zone read-only) and the generated Agent Teams table in CLAUDE.loa.md are removed. Two of them cite mechanized enforcers (team-skill-guard.sh and a PreToolUse:Write/Edit System Zone hook) and incident #337 / bridgebuilder-horizon-pr341 as source. The diff shown does not remove or re-home those enforcers or the LOA_TEAM_MEMBER checks that still appear in implement-gate.sh.
findings.failure_mode: Either the enforcement hooks persist with no constraint of record (lint/validate-constraints drift, undocumented asks for teammates), or they were removed and multi-agent sessions regain the #337 corruption paths (concurrent br/SQLite writes, concurrent .run state read-modify-write) with no prose rule left in CLAUDE.loa.md.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the PR where these rules moved (agent-teams-reference.md is in the omitted list) and confirm team-skill-guard.sh / the System Zone hook status matches; if the rules were only relocated from constraints.json to prose, keep at least C-TEAM-002/003 as constraints since they guard data integrity, not instruction budget.
